text: The third form of Navadurga: Sri Chandraghanta Devi
Why did the Goddess get the name Chandraghanta?
Chandraghanta Devi is one of the powerful forms of Mother Parvati.
A crescent moon resembling the shape of a bell is present on the Goddess's forehead.
The name Chandraghanta came because the shape of the moon resembles a bell.
What is the specialty of this form?
The Goddess appears seated on a lion, with ten hands.
In those hands are weapons like the trishula, sword, and mace.
This form offers fearlessness to devotees on one side, and is ready to confront evil forces on the other.
But in her hands are weapons of war.
This means being peaceful is not a weakness.
When necessary, one must also have the courage to confront unrighteousness.
Sri Chandraghanta Devi is the Goddess who displays these two qualities in one form.
